main_text.p: fcurabuntur, ftellæ è cælo decidét vel certè pro-pter defectû lucis, ita videbitur hominibus. De his signis vide Matth.24.29. Luc.21.25. ubi dici-tur, ex his agnoscedum, prope esse regnum Dei, h. e. instare adventum Domini. Ex his signis se-quuntura est insignis cômotio in hominibus, qui in advetu Domini fupererunt: Ac primû repro-bi homines præ timore exanimati ex expecta-tione eorû quæ evadent in orbe, passim latibula quærent, ut ab ira agni abscondantur. Luc.21.27. Apoc.6.16. & seq. {*}Refipifcetiâ autè tacti, amarè*Tanitentiâ quidé, id est, μετα- μελει- λειαν: sed non refipi- scentiâ, id est μετάνοια.[?] plangent super mortem Domini, quam peccatis suis procuraverût, tanquâ plancu[?] pro unigeni-to, Luc.21.28. Zach.13.11. & seq. Apoc.1.7. Nûc, ut de signis quæ cû ipso Domini adventu cojuncta erunt, dicamus: in ipso adventu ac defcenfu Do-mini de cælis, terribilis totius mundi per ignem flammanté erit disfolutio, ita ut donec renove-tur non appareat; {*}quæ signum Christi vocatur*Imò aliud, nempe ipse Christus. Matth.24.30. Primûm cçlorû erit disfolutio, qua conflagrantes ῥοιζηδὸν[?], id est, tanquâ rotularum stridore præteribunt. Deinde erit disfolutio ele-mentorum: nam elemeta omnia ęstuantia, & terra cum operibus quæ in eâ sunt, exusta disfolvêtur. De his vide Matth.24.30. 2. Pet.3.10.12. Apoc.20. 11. & 21.1. page.notes: Greek words in the text and notes (ῥοιζηδὸν, μετάνοια, μεταμέλεια) are uncertain; the Greek in the left-hand reference notes is read approximately. The word "plancu" is doubtful, as are "quuntura" and the marginal "tem / tanto" pair. "Quæ" and "Tanitentiâ" in the right margin are read from a small, slightly blurred scan. The printed asterisks and daggers are marked as reference symbols. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot of the page.
